--- title: "Data" --- ## Inputs | input | source | vintage | note | |---|---|---|---| | building footprints + heights | GlobalBuildingAtlas (TU Munich, PlanetScope-derived) | 2024 | 673,583 raw; height error 1.5–9 m | | building typology | Overture Maps POI matching | 2026 | 12 classes; ~35% evidence-supported, rest heuristic | | slum extents | mapped slums (KML) | 2016 | 2,542 polygons, 33.5 km² | | ward boundaries | BMC / open data | — | 24 wards | | ward population | MCGM civic demographics | mid-2023 | 13,014,389 | | income proxy | Maharashtra Annual Statement of Rates via public compilations | 2026–27 | 125 localities → ward medians | | weather | daily Tmax/Tmin | 1951–2024 | station era only (2020+) | | road network | OpenStreetMap via osmnx | 2026 | 6,157 km | ## Derived stock ::: {#758b5a96 .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
buildings in Greater Mumbai 580,890
floor area 279.7 km²
households 3.22 M
informal share of buildings 48.9%
``` ::: ::: ## The income proxy The eASR portal disallows automated access, so ward-level rates were derived from published compilations of the same official schedule: 125 revenue-village localities, manually mapped to wards with a confidence flag, then taken as a median per ward. The spread is 7.3× from M/East (₹53,970/m²) to A ward (₹3,92,624/m²), which is enough to define four meaningful income bands. It remains **land value, not income**. Its worst failure — informal settlements inside expensive wards, such as Dharavi in G/North or Behrampada in H/East — is handled by pinning slum-flagged buildings to the lowest band regardless of rate. ## The weather record The daily series splices two sources, visible in the decimal precision: 1951–2019 is a gridded product (April–May median Tmax ≈ 35.9 °C, daily range ≈ 12 °C), 2020–2024 is station data (34.5 °C, range ≈ 8.5 °C). The gridded era is inland-biased and would overstate cooling demand, so only the station era is used. A typical pre-monsoon day is taken as the April–May median and expanded to 24 hours with a Parton–Logan curve. One consequence: a single series means **no urban heat island gradient**. Every ward receives identical forcing, and the only spatial variation in indoor temperature comes from building fabric. ## Still to acquire | what | from | unlocks | |---|---|---| | AC ownership by income | CEEW India Residential Energy Survey, Maharashtra | calibration of the two dominant coefficients | | feeder / division load | AEML, BEST, Tata Power, MSEDCL | validation of the 3,064 MW baseline | | tariff slabs and time-of-day | MERC orders | electricity price in the adoption and runtime decisions | | traffic counts | MMRDA Comprehensive Transportation Study | the vehicle heat term, currently one invented number | | current slum extents | own Sentinel-2 classification | replaces the 2016 layer | | machine-readable ASR | IGR Maharashtra | replaces hand-transcribed localities |
